scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported 1492 to 1500 polygon lies along the lower Appomattox, consistent with this identity but not a verified contemporary boundary. The similarly named Northern Neck groups and Appomattox Court House are not this entry.
The NPS river article’s April 1607 visit is not adopted; the Library of Virginia gives 26 May. Percy’s 8 May encounter is a separate episode.
The 1610 phase avoids assigning a season to disputed attack chronology. A town’s destruction and a ruler’s death are not the community’s extinction.
The badge’s exact manufacture date, owner and excavation context are not established. No modern ceremonial object or distant archaeological site is substituted for local evidence.
The 1677 treaty memorandum explicitly excludes Pericuhtah despite the modern page’s signatory metadata. The expanded agreement is dated 1680 in the archival study.
Chapter 10 is a collection of documentary abstracts, distinct from chapter 4’s historical narrative. Ferry record dates are not sharpened beyond the published entries.
Bland is a colonizing outsider. His claims of discovery and mineral wealth are not accepted as new Indigenous discoveries or verified geology; the card attributes observations and explanations.
Regional Powhatan political patterns are labeled as context. No unsupported modern successor tribe or individual ancestry is assigned.
The ending remains uncertain beyond the documented early eighteenth-century community. Independent historical review, geometry review and depth certification remain pending.
